tasks.title: Implement overseer/actions.py (mode-gated action dispatch over injected seams)
acceptance_criteria: overseer/actions.py exists as a single whole-file, stdlib-only module.
Module-level ACTION_ROUTES dict maps mode name -> {command -> seam_key} and includes at least modes 'observe', 'brief-author', 'dispatch', and 'daemon-supervisor'.
Every mode key in ACTION_ROUTES exists in overseer.modes.MODE_REGISTRY.
Read-only modes (observe/analyze/audit) route ONLY to READ seam_keys; no command under a read-only mode maps to a write/mutating seam_key.
dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams) -> dict verifies mode authority FIRST: an unknown mode or out-of-mode command raises overseer.mode_gate.ModeViolation BEFORE any seam is touched.
On a valid command, dispatch_action resolves the seam via attribute access (seams.<seam_key>), calls it with args, and returns its dict result.
EXACTLY ONE seam fires on a valid command; ZERO seams fire on any rejection.
No test files are authored or edited; no other file is touched.

spec.objective: Build the NEW single-file, whole-file, stdlib-only module overseer/actions.py as an IMPL-only implementation against the pre-committed RED oracle tests/overseer/test_actions.py (AUTHORITATIVE). The module declares a mode->command->seam_key routing table (ACTION_ROUTES) and a dispatch_action entrypoint that enforces mode authority fail-closed before routing a permitted command to an EXISTING operator action via an injected seams bundle, keeping the tested surface free of real side effects.
functional_requirements: Define module-level ACTION_ROUTES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] mapping each mode name to a mapping of command -> seam_key, including at minimum the modes 'observe', 'brief-author', 'dispatch', and 'daemon-supervisor'.
Constrain ACTION_ROUTES so every mode key it declares also exists as a key in overseer.modes.MODE_REGISTRY.
Ensure ACTION_ROUTES['daemon-supervisor'] includes the command 'pause' mapped to an appropriate (mutating) seam_key.
Ensure read-only modes (observe/analyze/audit) map their commands ONLY to READ seam_keys, never to a write/mutating seam_key.

Implement dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams) -> dict that FIRST verifies the mode permits the command, raising overseer.mode_gate.ModeViolation for an unknown mode or an out-of-mode/unknown command before any seam is resolved or called.
On a valid (mode, command) pair, resolve the seam via getattr(seams, seam_key) and invoke it with args, returning the dict result it produces.
Guarantee exactly one seam fires for a valid command and zero seams fire for any rejection (fail-closed authority check precedes all side effects).
Import only overseer.mode_gate (for ModeViolation) and overseer.modes plus the Python standard library; introduce no new dependencies and touch no other file.
spec.interfaces: overseer/actions.py: dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams) -> dict; ACTION_ROUTES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] (mode -> {command -> seam_key}). Imports overseer.mode_gate (ModeViolation) and overseer.modes (MODE_REGISTRY).
edge_cases: Unknown mode passed to dispatch_action -> raises ModeViolation, no seam resolved/called.
Known mode but command not in that mode's route table -> raises ModeViolation before any seam call.

Valid command whose seam_key is missing on the injected seams bundle -> attribute resolution surfaces naturally (only after the authority check passes); authority check itself never depends on the seams bundle.
Read-only mode that would attempt a mutating route -> prevented by construction of ACTION_ROUTES (read-only modes only carry READ seam_keys).
'daemon-supervisor' 'pause' command routes to its mutating seam and returns that seam's dict result.
args is forwarded verbatim to the seam (no transformation), and the seam's returned dict is returned unchanged.
non_goals: No agent spawn, subprocess, model call, SSE, or network I/O.
No real operator action performed by the module itself; the injected seams bundle is the only side-effect path.
No authoring or editing of any test, including the oracle; the oracle is a pre-committed precondition.
No third-party dependencies; standard library only.
No changes to overseer.modes, overseer.mode_gate, or any file other than overseer/actions.py.
spec.implementation_notes:
Treat tests/overseer/test_actions.py as the authoritative contract. Enforce mode authority FIRST in dispatch_action so that ModeViolation is raised before any attribute access on seams, guaranteeing zero side effects on rejection. The oracle's RecordingSeams exposes one callable seam per seam_key via attribute access, so resolve with getattr(seams, seam_key) and call seam(args), returning its dict. Keep ACTION_ROUTES values (seam_keys) consistent with read-only vs mutating semantics so read-only modes never reference a write seam. Keep the module whole-file and stdlib-only; import ModeViolation from overseer.mode_gate and validate mode keys against overseer.modes.MODE_REGISTRY.

# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/overseer/test_actions.py
```python
"""RED oracle for overseer/actions.py — mode-gated action dispatcher.

dispatch_action enforces mode authority FIRST (fail-closed: an out-of-mode
command raises ModeViolation and NO seam fires), then routes the command to the
EXISTING operator action via an INJECTED seam, so the tested surface has zero
side effects. Read-only modes resolve only to read seams.
"""
import pytest

from overseer.mode_gate import ModeViolation
from overseer.actions import dispatch_action, ACTION_ROUTES


class RecordingSeams:
    """A seam bundle that records calls instead of performing real actions."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        def _seam(args):
            self.calls.append((key, args))
            return {"seam": key, "echo": args}
        return _seam

    def __contains__(self, key):
        return True


def test_action_routes_cover_representative_modes():
    # Each tier has at least one routable command, keyed by mode then command.
    assert "observe" in ACTION_ROUTES
    assert "brief-author" in ACTION_ROUTES
    assert "dispatch" in ACTION_ROUTES
    assert "daemon-supervisor" in ACTION_ROUTES
    # Every routed mode is a real mode.
    from overseer.modes import MODE_REGISTRY
    for mode in ACTION_ROUTES:
        assert mode in MODE_REGISTRY


def test_a_valid_command_invokes_the_seam_and_returns_a_dict():
    seams = RecordingSeams()
    mode = "brief-author"
    command = next(iter(ACTION_ROUTES[mode]))
    out = dispatch_action(mode, command, {"x": 1}, seams=seams)
    assert isinstance(out, dict)
    assert len(seams.calls) == 1  # exactly one seam fired


def test_out_of_mode_command_fails_closed_no_seam_fires():
    seams = RecordingSeams()
    # observe is read-only: an authoring command must be refused BEFORE any seam.
    with pytest.raises(ModeViolation):
        dispatch_action("observe", "author_brief", {"slug": "x"}, seams=seams)
    assert seams.calls == []


def test_unknown_mode_is_rejected_fail_closed():
    seams = RecordingSeams()
    with pytest.raises(ModeViolation):
        dispatch_action("no-such-mode", "anything", {}, seams=seams)
    assert seams.calls == []


def test_read_only_modes_only_route_to_read_seams():
    # No observe/analyze/audit command may map to a write/mutating seam.
    write_seam_keys = {
        "brief_author", "oracle_author", "dispatch", "triage",
        "daemon_lifecycle", "flag_steward", "harness_self_fix",
        "rebuild", "push",
    }
    for mode in ("observe", "analyze", "audit"):
        for command, seam_key in ACTION_ROUTES.get(mode, {}).items():
            assert seam_key not in write_seam_keys


def test_daemon_supervisor_pause_is_routable():
    # pause is the fail-safe direction and must always be available in-mode.
    seams = RecordingSeams()
    assert "pause" in ACTION_ROUTES["daemon-supervisor"]
    out = dispatch_action("daemon-supervisor", "pause", {}, seams=seams)
    assert isinstance(out, dict)
    assert seams.calls and seams.calls[0][0] is not None

```
